observations.text:
18-year-old me used to wake up at 5am so she had time to do yoga before school.
She would sit down in silence with the sunrise to a YouTube guided meditation. And to her, she found peace in that, even when she knew no one around her was doing similar practices. 

During the pandemic, tarot found her. She got a deck and went straight to intuitively reading the cards for her friends. “How was that so accurate?” “That’s definitely what I’m going through.” And she would secretly pull a card for herself and journal her reflections. Somehow, she found herself waking up at 5am again to do yoga, meditate to Dr Joe Dispenza, and gradually opened herself up to meeting her guides, even though she used to chant for her third eye to close in hopes of not seeing those things lurking in shadows. And from then on, she started to see the light with the gift and no longer the fear.

Diving more into introspection, countless afternoon meditations with an amethyst balancing on her forehead, and a few months in, she sat beside her cousin and childhood friend and burst out a suggestion: let’s go up to the rooftop and meditate. Just follow my voice.
They shared their visions and what they felt, and for her, it felt natural and she was also amazed of the simple presence shared in silence and deep breaths.

Then I moved abroad. More of this journey later… 

Photos from 2018-2021

#spiritualpath #spiritualawakening #spirituality

Almost a year ago, I officially launched Maria Fenton Coaching here in the UAE 🫢

And soon, it’ll be a year and a half since I left real estate!

Real estate was a big chapter of my life and one I’m really grateful for. It taught me so much about people, communication, sales, confidence and how to deal with uncomfortable situations. I genuinely don’t think I’d be the coach or business owner I am today without that experience.

But towards the end, I knew it wasn’t for me anymore.

The stress levels were high, I wasn’t dealing with it very well and even though it was a very well-paid career, I couldn’t ignore the feeling that there was something else I wanted to do.

For years, I had this little voice in the back of my head telling me I wanted to work for myself.

The idea excited me.
The reality terrified me 😂

There were plenty of moments where I questioned myself.

But if there’s one thing I’ve learned, it’s that growth rarely happens when you stay where it’s comfortable.

This business has given me so much more than I ever expected.

It’s given me confidence.
It’s challenged me.
It’s forced me to grow as a coach, as a business owner and as a person.

It’s given me the flexibility to travel more, spend more time with my family and prioritise my own health and wellbeing.

But the best part by far has been the women I’ve had the privilege of working with 🤍

So if you’ve ever supported my business, trusted me as your coach, shared my content or simply followed along on the journey, thank you!

Taking the leap was scary.
But looking back now, I’m so glad I did.

Here’s to year two ✨

observations.text:
9 rules for operating like an ambitious healthy Dubai CEO.

(From 10 years of coaching executives, founders, and entrepreneurs)

There are hundreds of health "guides" out there for busy professionals.

But not enough simple, actionable systems built for how executives actually live.

So here's the one I use with every client:

1. Treat your body like a business
↳ Get baseline data. Bloods, body comp, resting heart rate.
↳ If it doesn't get measured, it doesn't get managed.

2. Train at least 3x a week
↳ Three structured sessions beat six random ones. Every time.
↳ Leave reps in the tank. Consistency beats intensity.

3. Protect sleep like you protect your calendar
↳ 7+ hours. Non-negotiable.
↳ People who function on under six hours? Rounded up, that's zero.

4. Eat enough protein across 4 meals
↳ Your body can only absorb so much per sitting.
↳ A shake at 3pm and steak at 9 isn't a plan.

5. Build a decision framework for food
↳ Hotels, client dinners, airports. You need rules that travel.
↳ Rigid meal plans break. Frameworks survive anything.

6. Review your data weekly
↳ Weekly averages over daily weigh-ins. Always.
↳ One bad Tuesday is noise. An 8-week trend is signal.

7. Build recovery as a system
↳ Recovery and training volume need to match.
↳ One outgrows the other, you get under-recovered.

8. Set a 90-day body composition target
↳ Write it down. "From X kg to Y kg by this date."
↳ Vague goals get vague results. Be specific.

9. Build autonomy, not dependency
↳ The goal is results you can keep without a coach.
↳ If the system only works when someone runs it, it's not yours.

You don't need another app.
You don't need another supplement stack.

You need a system that ties the basics together and runs on data, not guesswork.

If you want to see how your current setup stacks up, take the Executive Physique Audit here: https://calendly.com/zofit/1-1-personal-training-video-session

It scores your training, nutrition, and recovery against what we use with clients.

Your health is your choice.

Make the right one

Z

'I eat healthy but cannot lose weight'

As a fitness professional of 11 wonderful years, I eat by one rule:

High protein. Controlled calories. Minimum prep.

***Here's the exact daily nutrition framework I use to hit 200g of protein in 10 minutes a day:***

You need a structure you can repeat.

Meal 1: The Greek Yogurt Protein Bowl

▫️ 200g fat-free Greek yogurt
▫️ 1 scoop whey protein
▫️ Handful of blueberries
▫️ Sprinkle of cinnamon + drizzle of honey

380 cals | 48g protein

Tastes like dessert. Takes 3 minutes. Elite protein.

Meal 2:  Elite Chicken Bowl:

▫️ 250g chicken breast (air fryer, smoked paprika, garlic powder, salt)
▫️ 1 microwave rice cup
▫️ Handful of spinach + lemon juice

510 cals | 75g protein

Air fryer cooks, Microwave rice saves time. 

Season chicken and it's elite.

Meal 3: 5-Minute Shrimp Stir-Fry:

▫️ 200g prawns/shrimp (frozen → pan, 4 mins)
▫️ Frozen stir-fry veg mix
▫️ Splash soy sauce + garlic + chilli flakes
▫️ Squeeze of lime

280 cals | 55g protein

Prawns cook in minutes from frozen. 

Tastes like takeaway without the calories.

Snack Options: The Protein Hit (anytime)

▫️ 150g Lean Beef Jerky (split across the day)
▫️ 1 Cup Cottage Cheese + Berries + Cinnamon
▫️ 150g Sliced Turkey + Mustard + Pepper + Cucumber

230 cals | 38g protein

Stock up at work, or home.

Zero prep. 

High protein.

Daily Total:

→ Calories: ~1,900
→ Protein: 250g
→ Total prep time: Under 10 minutes

That leaves you ~300 spare calories for:

▫️ A piece of fruit
▫️ A handful of nuts
▫️ A coffee with milk
▫️ Or nothing, bank it for a bigger deficit

You're hitting 150g+ protein with room to spare. 
Every single day.

"But I'll get bored eating the same thing."

You won't, because you rotate flavour, not structure:

Chicken breast swaps (same cook time):

▫️ Monday: Smoked paprika + garlic powder
▫️ Tuesday: Cajun seasoning + lime
▫️ Wednesday: Italian herbs + balsamic glaze
▫️ Thursday: Soy sauce + sesame + ginger
▫️ Friday: Lemon pepper + oregano

Same protein. 
Same macros. 
Completely different meal every day. 
Zero extra time.

Wasn’t sure if I was going to do @burj2burj today. 

After having surgery 5 weeks ago and my head is still numb. 
I haven’t been able to do much training for it after having a little hiatus. 
Then medication making me unwell and my immune system being really low and excessive fatigued. 
I was not expecting to do it. 

Even my Garmin has told me my recovery is really low and to listen to my body (which I do most of the time). Don’t usually listen to my watch mind 😅

But when I woke up today I felt better and recovery was good, so I thought let’s just show up. 

I wasn’t aiming for a specific time. 

When I signed up my goal was sub 1.45 hrs.

Today my goal was to finish. 

And we did just that. 

Not a PB, last year I managed 1.47.20

This year 1.48.39.

observations.author: self
observations.text:
Today marks 8 years in Dubai. #dubaianniversary 

Crazy how time really flies. 

It’s tested me in many ways, so many that I nearly gave up the dubai life last year, but 2026 I’m still here, you can really never be certain of anything in life.

The weather 🤣
Your Health 
Relationships 
Friendships 
Timing 
People 
Jobs 

But I am certain of my ability to keep going no matter what life throws at me. I will continue to adapt, especially when it feels uncomfortable! 
Because we all know the saying “Growth doesn’t happen in comfort zones” 😉

Which honestly is challenging because I don’t know how to sit still and my mind is 100 miles a minute! But again we learning.
That is the beauty of life! Continuing to learn. 

And I’m learning to stay true to myself and I will always honor my integrity. 
I still care, I still love, I still show up, but not at the expense of my own truth.

Happy anniversary Dubai 

Love always K 🤍

observations.text:
According to Sternberg’s theory, the balance of intimacy, passion, and commitment naturally shifts and evolves over the course of a relationship.

While passion tends to peak quickly before declining and levelling off, and commitment peaks and remains relatively stable, intimacy requires ongoing sharing and emotional connection.

Sternberg emphasizes that relationships are generally at their happiest and most stable when the strength and need of these various three components are similar between both partners.
